headline: High-risk shared-write and unverified-output pathways make CrewAI→Langflow pair dangerous by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and uses shared memory by default; Langflow reads uploaded/server files and can chain agents. That creates a plausible file-based instruction bridge where content from one can influence the other. The pathway is not proven to be a direct parser hijack, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF CrewAI writes attacker-controlled text into a shared workspace that Langflow later ingests as flow input
IF Langflow components treat file contents as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable automatic file ingestion in Langflow
Add content provenance labels before handoff
Require manual review of any file passed between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, while Langflow touches flow inputs, intermediate outputs, and stored component credentials. Both have filesystem access and broad network egress, so shared deployment can expose sensitive data across the pair. The blast radius is more than one artifact, but no evidence shows uncontrollable third-party exfiltration by default.
conditions: IF both agents run in the same host workspace or shared server-side store
IF sensitive crew data or flow credentials are written to files accessible by the other agent
mitigations: Use separate OS users or containers
Store secrets in distinct vaults
Restrict filesystem permissions on shared directories
Turn off persistence for intermediate outputs
Audit logs for cross-agent file reads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write and broad subprocess/network capability, and neither profile shows locking or coordination. CrewAI uses per-process shared state defined by the developer, while Langflow uses server-side state and stores; if pointed at the same mutable directory or resource, concurrent writes can corrupt state or overwrite outputs. Uncertainty about deployment should not lower severity.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, database, or object store
IF no external lock or transaction boundary is configured
mitigations: Assign disjoint write paths
Enable file or DB locking
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Mount shared storage read-only for one agent
Use per-run namespaces for server-side state

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI can emit tool outputs and shared-memory results that Langflow can chain into downstream nodes. Langflow’s graph-based flows can treat upstream outputs as inputs, so a mistaken or malicious CrewAI result may propagate into later actions without verification. The pair does not prove automatic action-taking, so medium fits rather than high.
conditions: IF Langflow nodes consume CrewAI output without a validation step
IF downstream flow nodes act on that output by sending requests or triggering tools
mitigations: Insert a validation node between agents
Require schema checks on all handoffs
Mark CrewAI outputs as untrusted by default
Add human approval before side-effecting nodes

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, while Langflow stores per-flow credentials and processes flow inputs/intermediate outputs. If regulated data is routed through both, differing storage locations and retention behaviors can create a compliance mismatch. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so the safest supported judgment is medium, not low.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are placed into both systems
IF one deployment retains logs or stored credentials longer than the other
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both systems
Align retention settings before deployment
Document data flow and residency
Purge stored credentials after each run
Review access logs for regulated fields
